messages.content: Use at least 4.0 different coordinating conjunctions in the response. This delayed obliteration of the arterial lumen may occur by one of several mechanisms. The roughened or torn arterial intima attracts platelets, fibrin, and red cells, resulting in a traumatic thrombosis. On occasion, the flow of blood may elevate the torn distal end of the intima, creating a subintimal dissection and lifting an intimal flap that occludes the distal lumen. Moreover, even though the inner and outer coats of the artery remain intact, an intramural hematoma may form that obliterates the lumen of the artery..  explain more
